title: The Role of Body Language in Corporate Personality Assessments
author: HR Workshop Lead
excerpt: Your posture, hand gestures, and tone of voice communicate more than your words. Learn the exact executive body language cues to crack interviews.
body:
In modern corporate recruitment, hiring managers assess candidates far beyond their resumes. During interviews and group discussions, your non-verbal cues—specifically posture, hand gestures, and eye contact—communicate your confidence, competence, and leadership potential before you even finish your first sentence.

Here is a guide to mastering corporate body language cues for professional career growth:

1. The Power Posture: Always sit straight with your shoulders relaxed. Slouching projects disinterest or a lack of confidence, while leaning too far back can look arrogant. A slight forward tilt indicates high engagement and active listening.

2. The Eye Contact Matrix: Maintain eye contact for 60-70% of the conversation. Too much eye contact can appear aggressive, while looking down or away repeatedly suggests evasion or anxiety. When speaking to a panel, address each member sequentially.

3. Expressive Hand Gestures: Use open-palm gestures to convey honesty and receptivity. Restrict your gestures to the 'steeple' shape (fingertips touching) to project authority. Avoid crossing your arms, which acts as a subconscious barrier suggesting defensiveness.

4. Controlled Speaking Pace: Under stress, the body releases adrenaline, causing candidates to speak rapidly in a high pitch. Practice pausing for one second before answering and lower your speaking register to convey executive presence.

Through our specialized weekly Personality Development sessions at GLA, candidates participate in mock group debates, body language analysis under video recordings, and professional presentation rehearsals. Capping batches at 5-7 students ensures personalized coaching for every student.
